symptom: Argument cleanup creates a false internal tail call (major, 1 instance, crackmes.one 5ab77f5f33c5d40ad448c820). Classified the jump at 0x4010f2 as a tail call after ADD ESP,8 removes two call arguments. Its destination, 0x401102, is an internal TEST EAX,EAX reached by both paths; saved registers remain on the stack.
decisions: The filed hypothesis -- 'frame matching may confuse argument cleanup with restoration of saved registers' -- is exactly right and is recorded as confirmed, not overturned. tailcallframe's backward scan stops at the first control-flow op, so on the witness it measures the `add esp,8` in front of the branch and stops at the `call 0x40167d` above it, never seeing the two argument pushes that the cleanup undoes. The entry run is `push ebx; push esi` (-8) and the cleanup is +8, so the exact-cancellation test is satisfied by two unrelated stack motions.

Not covered by an existing option. `kuna catalog --json` has one option in this family, `tailcallframe` itself (DIV-109), and turning it off closes the witness only by giving up the capability it exists for: the round-2 keyboard-callback witness (tailcallframe_x86_64 on_key at 0x11b0) regresses to inlining its callee. So this is a narrowing of that predicate, not a default flip.

Chose the ABI invariant over the two alternatives considered. (a) Scanning backward THROUGH a call, accounting it as SP-neutral, would also reject the residual `sub esp,N` shape, but it is unsound on exactly this binary class: a stdcall callee cleans its own arguments with `ret N`, so a call is not SP-neutral on Windows PE, and a noreturn callee never restores anything. (b) Rejecting any epilogue run terminated by a CALL would break a real and common shape -- gcc -O2 emits `sub rsp,8; call f; add rsp,8; jmp g` -- which the chosen rule keeps, because a frame built purely by `sub rsp,N` saves no register and so demands none back.

The rule cannot create a false negative on a genuine tail call: the ABI requires every callee-saved register the prologue pushed to be restored before the jump, so `restored >= saved` holds for any real tail-call epilogue. Verified on both existing tailcallframe witnesses (the round-2 fixture `push rbp`/`pop rbp`, and tests/stages/tailcallframe.xml `push rbx; sub rsp,0x10` / `add rsp,0x10; pop rbx`), both of which still fire.

Known residual, not papered over: a frame built purely by `sub esp,N` whose N happens to equal a cdecl argument cleanup in front of the branch still matches, because with no register saved there is nothing to ask for. Closing that needs the flow-ordering change tailcallframe's own module header already names as the sound fix.

decbench.method: whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` A/B, `--option tailcallsaved off` (byte-identical to the pre-change tree, since the gate is the only behavioural difference) vs default
decbench.note: Every decbench binary is a gcc-built ELF, almost all x86-64 SysV, where there is no cdecl argument cleanup to misread. This arm proves no collateral; it does not exercise the rule.

crackme_pe.method: same A/B over the RE-friction dataset and the repipe probe corpus, where the shape actually occurs (32-bit cdecl PE). Stopped early for time at 371 of 609 inputs; 228 of those fail to load on BOTH arms (rc equal, so not caused by this change).
hunk_notes: All 33 internal cases are the defect: a `jmp` after `call f; add esp,N` was recovered as a call to a block of the same function, truncating it. Read in full: Silvers-CrackMe-1 sub_44a2d0 (two false calls to 0x44a3a5 and 0x44a3c3, now one coherent function) and sub_44eb61 (two false calls to 0x44ed30/0x44ed32; the fixed version has real `return 0;` / `return 0xffffffff;` paths).

The one 'gained' case is the largest win in the sweep: crkme.exe sub_4047e4 was the single line `sub_4047f6();` -- a call to its own second instruction -- and is now the whole 313-line polymorphic decryptor. The three tail calls it 'gained' are inside that body, which did not exist before.

pcme0 sub_8048ace: the declined target 0x8048d03 is a duplicated `mov eax,1; int 0x80` exit stub a few bytes further into the same routine (the classifier called it external only because the next LISTED entry sorts lower). One line moves, from `sub_8048d03();` to `(*(void *)swi(0x80))();`. Neutral.

The one observed non-improvement: illusion.exe sub_40be3d, an anti-analysis binary whose function is garbage on both arms (`Control flow encountered bad instruction data`, a 14 KB stack array, `Stackfffffff8`). The declined target 0x8850147d is outside the image entirely, so `tailcallframe` had been ending the decode on a garbage jump; without it kuna follows the jump and reports `Function flows into unmapped memory`. Both renderings are junk; the change swaps which failure is reported. Declining an unmapped destination is `tailcallframe`'s question, not this predicate's, and is left alone.

speed_method: whole-binary `decompile-all` of openssh-portable/sftp (O2, 872 KB), 5 interleaved rounds alternating arm order after one warmup, medians; output byte-identical between arms
speed_note: Indistinguishable from noise. The single-function timeit on the witness itself reports +38.9%, which is not the predicate's cost: with the option ON the function is no longer truncated at a false tail call, so the ON arm decompiles the whole classifier and the OFF arm decompiles about half of it.
tests: tests/stages/kuna-tailcallsaved.xml (two-pass: option off = the bug, default = the fix)
